title: GLP-1s Slow Aging: Reaction Short Options
sub: Future reaction short, not on any shoot doc. Two clips for one short about the new GLP-1 aging study. Pick one. Built 2026-10-19.
decisions: Do not react to the Newsweek article itself. It is text on a page with a stock photo of a pen. There is no person taking a position, so nothing for you to answer.

Better video found: ABC News, Oct 14. A Harvard doctor on national TV says the anti-aging results are only in mice and he would not take a GLP-1 for anti-aging. He is wrong about the mice, and the study proves it. That gives the short a payoff.
Skipped the local news reads (Fox 13 Utah, WSMV Nashville, KVUE Austin). 30 seconds of an anchor reading the facts, no position. Same problem as the article.

Backup clip: Bryan Johnson, "olive oil is better than Ozempic". The biggest name in anti-aging, saying something you can knock down with this study. Bigger name than the ABC doctor, but the clip is from Dec 2024 and it is not about this study.

The facts, so the script gets them right. The 2 to 4 years is the HEART result for semaglutide (Ozempic, Wegovy): Novo Nordisk scientists tested blood proteins from 10,052 people in five randomized trials, drug against placebo. Other organs (kidney, brain, pancreas, lung) came out 1 to 4 years younger. Weight loss did not fully explain it. Lilly separately found tirzepatide (Zepbound) users tested younger too, in a smaller group of 71 people over 50. Neither study is peer-reviewed yet, and the drugmakers ran both.
Not added to any shooting document. When you want it filmed, a scripting task turns the kept card into a full script.

items.t: ABC News Doctor Says Ozempic Only Slows Aging In Mice. He's Wrong.
items.src: ABC News, "Measles, GLP-1s and anti-aging: How to protect your health" (Oct 14, 2026)
items.words: Starts on "Some research calling them potential anti-aging drugs. Is this for real?". Ends on "I would not take a GLP-1 drug for anti-aging."
items.what: ABC News anchor asks Dr. Raj Panjabi, a Harvard doctor plugging his new book, whether the GLP-1 anti-aging research is real. He says the studies are early, they are in mice, they are not peer-reviewed, and he would not take a GLP-1 for anti-aging.
pts: Hook (your first words after the clip): "He's wrong. This wasn't mice. It was more than 10,000 people."

My take: Novo Nordisk tested the blood of 10,052 people in five randomized trials, the drug against a placebo. On Ozempic, the heart tested 2 to 4 years younger. Kidneys, brain, pancreas and lungs, 1 to 4 years younger. Lilly found the same thing with tirzepatide, the drug in Zepbound. He's right about one thing: it isn't peer-reviewed yet.
The part nobody is saying: weight loss alone didn't explain it. Something else in these drugs is making your organs younger.

Lesson: Belly fat is what ages you. Taking a low dose to get lean and stay lean is the anti-aging. Your facts: 192 to 175 in 3 months, 1.5 mg a week, on it for life, and a low dose helps nearly every man.

Bottom line: "I don't take Zepbound to look younger. I take it to stay lean. Now it turns out staying lean on it may be making my heart younger too." Close: "If you want to learn how I use Zepbound to stay lean, subscribe to my channel."
items.note: Risk: you killed the GMA doctor on stopping Ozempic as "boring, not someone I care about". This is a TV doctor too, so the clip lives or dies on his "they're in mice" line, which is the hard position you are knocking down. The verdict "He's wrong" is my reading from your record (Zepbound for life), not something you have said about this study. On-screen graphic idea: "10,052 people. 5 trials. Heart 2 to 4 years younger." in Soft Blue.

items.t: Bryan Johnson Says Olive Oil Is Better Than Ozempic. He's Wrong.
items.src: More Plates More Dates, "Olive Oil Is Better Than Ozempic" with Bryan Johnson (Dec 2024)
items.words: Starts on "Look at the evidence we just shared". Ends on "It's better than Ozempic. Really, it is."
items.what: Bryan Johnson, the tech millionaire known for spending millions a year trying to reverse his age, doubles down on his claim that extra virgin olive oil is better than Ozempic.
pts: Hook (your first words after the clip): "The guy who spends millions trying to stay young just told you to skip the one drug that's been shown to make your heart younger."

My take: A tablespoon of olive oil is 120 calories. Pouring more of it on your food doesn't take fat off, it adds it. Meanwhile Ozempic's own trials, 10,052 people, drug against placebo: the heart tested 2 to 4 years younger.

Lesson: If you're carrying belly fat, getting lean is the anti-aging, and a low dose is the fastest way there. Your facts: 192 to 175 in 3 months on 1.5 mg a week. Olive oil is fine on a salad. It is not a weight loss drug.

Bottom line: "Bryan has the money for every anti-aging trick on earth, and he's betting on salad dressing. I'll take the shot." Close: "If you want to learn how I use Zepbound to stay lean, subscribe to my channel."
items.note: Check by ear: the clip should start on Bryan's voice, not the host quoting him (captions put the handover near 3:34). You have no position on record about Bryan Johnson, so the verdict is my guess. Bryan's 5.2 pounds in 9 weeks olive oil number is his claim and I could not check it, so the reaction does not use it.
